# Konspec UI

> Copy-paste HTML components for internal data applications. Light theme only. A component library written for the agent building your app.

You are reading the entry point for this design system. It is written for agents.
Read all of it before writing markup for a Konspec application, then fetch the
variants you need one at a time from /r/ and copy their markup verbatim.
Do not fetch registry.json: it is the whole system in one response and will
not fit in your context. The Machine-readable section at the end has the
endpoints and what each one costs.

## Protocol

1. **Read llms.txt** — The stack, the tokens and the hard rules in one file, generated from the same source as this page. It is short. Read all of it.
   `GET /llms.txt`
2. **Fetch one variant at a time and copy verbatim** — The response body of a variant endpoint is the markup itself: no JSON envelope, no escaping, nothing to parse. Copy the string. Do not paraphrase markup you have already been handed, and do not reformat it into your own idiom. llms.txt lists every component with its variant ids, so once you have read it you can build these URLs yourself and never need an index. Fetch r/<id>.json when you need a component's rules, anatomy or accessibility notes rather than its markup, and r/index.json only if you arrived without reading llms.txt.
   `GET /r/<id>/<variant>.html  →  the markup, ready to paste`
3. **Never fetch registry.json** — It still exists and is still generated, so nothing that already points at it breaks, but it is the entire system in one response and it will not fit in your context: a few megabytes, several times a 200k window. An agent that fetches it gets a truncated file, and a truncated registry is worse than none, because the components that survived the cut look complete and the ones that did not look absent. This is stated as its own step because an agent told only to use the new endpoints will reach for the old file the moment the new ones look incomplete.
   `// use /r/ — registry.json is back-compat only`
4. **Match the reference implementation** — A complete procurement dashboard built only from these components. When the docs and a real screen disagree about spacing or hierarchy, the screen wins.
   `GET /reference/`
5. **Ask rather than choose** — If a colour, size, pattern, component or layout is not defined here, it does not exist yet. Stop and flag it rather than filling the gap yourself: name what is missing and what it has to do, and let a person add it to the framework. Adding one is a decision for a person, not a default you pick because the page looked empty. An invented component is worse than a blocked screen, because it ships, gets copied, and never gets the accessibility work. This covers missing variants of components that do exist, not just missing components.
   `// no new tokens, components or layouts without a human`

## Stack

- **css**: Tailwind CSS v4 — utility classes only. No component CSS, no @apply, no custom colour tokens.
- **js**: Alpine.js 3 for local UI state, plus two official plugins — @alpinejs/collapse for animated panels and @alpinejs/focus for dialog focus traps. Both load before Alpine core. State lives on the component root, never in a global store.
- **server**: htmx for partial swaps. Alpine does not fetch.
- **charts**: Chart.js 4 via CDN, pinned, and only on pages that plot something. Colours are read out of the DOM at init, never written as hex: series from the HTML legend swatches, grid from the card border.
- **icons**: Lucide via CDN — <i data-lucide="name"></i>, hydrated by lucide.createIcons().
- **build**: None. Snippets are plain HTML and paste into Django, Flask or a static file unchanged.

## Rules

Every one of these exists because breaking it produced a visible defect at
least once. They are not style preferences.

1. **Use what is already here.** Before writing any markup, look for it in the component list in llms.txt. If a component or a page layout is already defined, copy its markup from /r/<id>/<variant>.html — writing your own version of something the registry defines is the defect this rule exists to prevent, because two implementations of one thing drift apart and only one of them ever gets the accessibility work. The layout entries are mandatory, not examples: a screen with a title and actions is page-header, a create-or-edit screen is form-page, and a queue worked one record at a time is list-detail. The shell that holds all of them is the next rule, and it is not optional. If what you need is not here, stop and flag it: name the thing, say what it has to do, and let a person add it to the framework. Do not invent a component, a layout or a pattern to fill the gap, and do not ship a one-off approximation of one under another name. A missing entry is a decision for a person; an invented one is a defect that ships and then gets copied. The same applies one level down, to variants: if the component is here but the variant you need is not, flag that too. Changing the labels, figures and records inside a variant is expected and is what copying it is for; reshaping one into a state, density or arrangement the registry does not list is a new variant, and a new variant is an addition to the framework rather than a local edit.
2. **Every signed-in screen is app-shell.** This is the one layout decision that is already made, and it is not a default you may weigh against alternatives. If a signed-in user can reach the page, the page is app-shell with the screen's own content inside <main>, copied from /r/app-shell/default.html like any other component. There are exactly two exceptions, auth-page and error-page, and they are exceptions for a reason rather than by taste: the shell reads the navigation, the counts and the signed-in user out of context that a signed-out visitor or a failed request may not have. Do not assemble a shell of your own out of sidebar and topbar. Those entries document the shell's parts and exist so its own variants can be built; a hand-rolled sidebar-plus-topbar is a second implementation of app-shell, and two implementations of one thing drift apart while only one of them keeps the accessibility work. Do not ship a lighter shell for one screen, and do not start a page at <main> because the screen looked simple enough not to need chrome. The shell owns the skip link, the nav landmark, the off-canvas focus trap, the collapse persistence, the command palette and the keyboard shortcuts; a page that skips it loses every one of them silently and still reviews as fine, because everything it dropped is invisible until somebody uses a keyboard or a phone. The test is the response, not the screen: if a signed-in request returns a page, it is app-shell. An htmx partial swapped into a shell already on screen is not a page and must not repeat it.
3. **Keep the data-kui attribute.** Every variant's root element carries data-kui="<component>/<variant>" — badge/table, app-shell/default. It is the only way to find, in an application nobody has touched for a year, which markup came from this framework and which entry it came from: grep data-kui across the repo and every pasted component answers for itself. Keep it on the element you copied it onto, keep the value exactly as the registry gives it, and do not add one by hand to markup that is not a copy of that variant — a wrong id is worse than none, because the next person updating that component will trust it. It is inert: no styling, no behaviour, no script reads it at runtime. Updating from it is something you do when a person asks for it and never on your own initiative: grep data-kui across the application, and for each hit fetch /r/<component>/<variant>.html, which is always the current markup for that entry, and diff it against the pasted copy. Nothing records which copies are stale, and nothing needs to — the diff is the answer. What you carry across is the class list and the structure. What you leave alone is everything the application put there: the labels, the template variables and tags, the hx-* attributes, the Alpine state and handlers, the ids and the form field names. A component is a shape, not content, so replacing a pasted block wholesale with the registry version silently deletes the work that made it a real screen. Where the two disagree on structure rather than on classes, stop and say so rather than reshaping the copy to match: the local version may have been changed deliberately, and that is a question for a person.
4. **Stock Tailwind only.** No custom CSS, no @theme colours, no arbitrary hex. Arbitrary values are for one-off sizes, never for colour.
5. **Light theme only.** There is no dark mode and none is planned. A second theme doubles the review surface for no benefit in an office tool.
6. **Never bind Alpine on a Lucide icon.** createIcons() replaces the <i> with an <svg>, destroying any :class on it. Bind on a wrapping span instead.
7. **Never add cursor-pointer.** Tailwind v4 preflight drops it from buttons. One base rule fixes every element; 300 utility classes do not.
8. **Colour means data state.** Red, amber and green describe what a record is doing. Never decoration, never a brand accent. They appear as a dot or an icon, never as a field of colour behind text.
9. **The accent is graphite.** zinc-700. Interactive text is zinc-900 plus an underline, not a colour.
10. **Alerts are neutral.** White card, zinc border, colour only in the icon. A full-width red field shouts louder than the overdue rows it describes.
11. **Focus is an outline, never a ring.** ring-* compiles to box-shadow, and forced-colours mode drops every box-shadow, so a ring is the one focus style guaranteed to vanish for the users who most need it. Write focus-visible:outline-3 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-zinc-700/15, and take the negative offset when the control sits flush inside a scroller that would clip it. outline-none is allowed only on a field whose wrapper draws the outline for it, because Tailwind resolves outline-style through a variable: outline-none on the same element kills its own focus outline while leaving the width and colour set, which measures as styled and renders as nothing.
12. **Every tinted shape carries its ring.** A tinted shape is bg-zinc-200 with ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300 — pills, chips, avatars, icon wells, control tracks, the selected nav item, all of them. A tinted surface is bg-zinc-100 — the page, a selected row, the highlighted option in a menu — and a band recessed inside a white surface is bg-zinc-50, which is a table header or a zebra row. Give a shape the surface fill and it measures 1.00 contrast against the surface it sits on, which is not low contrast but the identical colour, and it disappears. One step of fill separates them and the ring holds the edge. Solid shapes need no ring, and it is ring rather than border so adding it reflows nothing.
13. **Status colour lives in the dot.** Every status pill is the same graphite shape — bg-zinc-200, ring-zinc-300, zinc-700 text, the same fill an avatar takes. What separates Open from Overdue is a 6px dot. A column of tinted pills reads as a traffic light and stops meaning anything by the twelfth row; a column of identical pills with one red dot in it reads at a glance. This is the alert rule — colour only in the marker — applied to a pill.
14. **One shade per meaning.** Info is zinc-400, success emerald-600, warning amber-700, danger red-600 — and a warning is amber-700 in a component and amber-500 only when it is a dot, because a 1.5px stroke and a 6px disc need different weights of the same colour. Nothing takes a -50 tint or a -200 ring: a coloured icon well is still bg-zinc-200 with ring-zinc-300. Pick the shade from the token table, never by eye.
15. **Survive 390px.** Tables become stacked cards. Nothing scrolls sideways on a phone, with one exception: a carousel, where the sideways scroll is the component itself, and which snaps and peeks so it never looks like a layout that broke.
16. **No template x-for inside svg.** It is parsed in the SVG namespace and has no .content. Use divs, or a conic-gradient for donuts.
17. **x-cloak on anything hidden at first paint.** Alpine boots after the HTML renders. Without it, every dropdown flashes on load.
18. **Every text size carries its leading.** text-[13px] compiles to font-size alone — arbitrary sizes emit no line-height, so the element silently inherits whatever an ancestor left. Always write the slash form, text-[13px]/5. Sizes come from the seven steps; only prose may take a looser leading than the default pairing.
19. **Guard the Lucide re-hydration loop.** createIcons() leaves data-lucide on the <svg> it generates, so re-running it on every DOM mutation re-renders every icon forever. Guard on document.querySelector("[data-lucide]:not(svg)") or animations stutter while the DOM never settles.

## Tokens

Stock Tailwind. The class name is the token — there is no theme file to import.

### Surfaces

- **Page** `bg-zinc-100` — The scrolling page behind everything. Nothing inside a white surface may take this fill — same hex twice is a 1.00 contrast, and the card reads as a hole.
- **Surface** `bg-white` — Cards, panels, sidebar, topbar, table bodies.
- **Recessed** `bg-zinc-50` — A band inside a white surface: table header, zebra row. Lighter than the page, so it can never be read as the page showing through.
- **Edge** `border-zinc-300` — The outer edge of anything sitting on the page. White on zinc-100 is 1.10 and a zinc-200 edge is the first thing a washed-out panel drops.
- **Border** `border-zinc-200` — Edges inside a surface: inputs, a strip that ends a region, a nested panel.
- **Divider** `border-zinc-100` — Rows inside a card that is already bordered. On white only — on any tinted surface it computes to the surface.

### Text

- **Primary** `text-zinc-900` — Headings, values, anything you read first.
- **Secondary** `text-zinc-600` — Labels, descriptions, secondary copy.
- **Tertiary** `text-zinc-500` — Timestamps, hints, placeholder text.
- **On dark** `text-zinc-400` — The scale inverts on a zinc-900 band — the footer, the agent handoff. Darkening secondary text there makes it less readable, not more.

### Accent

- **Solid** `bg-zinc-700` — Primary buttons, progress fills, chart bars, the active nav marker.
- **Hover** `bg-zinc-800` — Hover state of anything accent-filled.
- **Tint** `bg-zinc-100` — A selected row, the highlighted option in a menu — surfaces, never shapes.
- **Chip** `bg-zinc-200` — Every tinted shape: badges, avatars, icon wells, control tracks, the selected nav item. One step deeper than the page so it keeps a fill of its own on either surface, and one deeper again for its ring.
- **Link** `text-zinc-900 underline underline-offset-2` — Interactive text. Colour is not the signal — the underline is.

### Semantic colour

One shade per meaning, and the same shade in every component. Pick from this
table rather than by eye. No -50 tints, no coloured rings — a coloured icon
well is still bg-zinc-200 with ring-zinc-300.

| tone | icon | mark you read | dot or bar | means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Info | `info` | `text-zinc-500` | — | Neutral notice. Grey, because nothing is wrong. |
| Success | `check-circle-2` | `text-emerald-600` | `bg-emerald-600` | Finished, posted, sent. Same green as the Closed dot. |
| Warning | `alert-triangle` | `text-amber-700` | `bg-amber-500` | Waiting, expiring, over a limit. 700 for marks you read — a 1.5px amber-500 stroke on white is illegible. |
| Danger | `alert-circle` | `text-red-600` | `bg-red-600` | Overdue, failed, destructive. Same red as the Overdue dot. |

### Typography

Inter and JetBrains Mono, self-hosted at assets/fonts.css. Nothing is fetched
from a font CDN at runtime.

Arbitrary font sizes compile to a font-size with no line-height, so every size
is written in the slash form and the pairing below is the default.

- `text-[11px]/4` — uppercase labels, counts, badge text
- `text-[12px]/4` — help text, timestamps, secondary lines
- `text-[13px]/5` — buttons, table cells, default component text
- `text-[14px]/5` — body copy, inputs, prose
- `text-[16px]/6` — card, dialog and panel titles
- `text-[20px]/7` — section headings, error page titles
- `text-[24px]/7` — page titles, KPI figures

Three weights, and no others:

- `font-normal` (400) — body copy, table cells, anything you read as a sentence
- `font-medium` (500) — anything that labels or acts — buttons, table headers, alert titles, nav items
- `font-semibold` (600) — headings, KPI figures, panel titles

Two tracking values, plus the default:

- `tracking-wider` — 11px uppercase labels only
- `tracking-tight` — headings at 20px and above
- `normal` — everywhere else. No arbitrary em values.

### Shape

- rounded-lg controls; rounded-xl panels; rounded-full pills; 36–44px control height.
- Every number gets tabular-nums, without exception. Columns of figures that do not line up are a bug.

## Status colours

Fixed. Do not reinterpret per screen. Colour describes what the record is
doing; the accent is graphite precisely so these stay meaningful.

| status | pill | dot | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-zinc-500` | The ordinary case |
| Approved | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-amber-500` | Waiting on someone |
| Overdue | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-red-600` | The alarm state |
| Closed | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-emerald-600` | Finished |
| Draft | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-600 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-zinc-400` | Not real yet |

## Components

One line each, with the variant ids that entry has. The markup for one variant
is at /r/<id>/<variant>.html and the rules, anatomy and accessibility notes for
a component are at /r/<id>.json. Fetch those before building anything, rather
than reconstructing a component from the one-line description here: the
description tells you which one to fetch, not what it looks like.

This list is a closed set, not a starting point. If what you are about to build
is on it, you must build it from the registry entry rather than from scratch.
That applies hardest to Layout: those entries are whole screens, and a screen
that is one of them is assembled from that entry, not redrawn.

If what you need is not on this list, it does not exist yet. Stop and flag it —
name the thing and what it has to do, and let a person add it to the framework.
Do not invent a component or a layout, and do not approximate one out of the
parts of another. Handing back a screen with a gap and a question is correct;
handing back a screen with an invented component in it is not.

Variants work the same way. Each entry below lists the variant ids it has, and
that list is closed too. Editing the labels, figures and records inside a
variant is expected. Reshaping one into a state, density or arrangement that is
not listed is a new variant, so flag it and let a person add it rather than
keeping it to yourself in one screen.

### Actions

- **Button** `button` — The standard action control. Exactly one primary button per view; everything else is secondary, ghost or a link. Variants: variants, sizes, icons, states, link, full-width, toolbar, django.
- **Button group** `button-group` — Several controls joined into one object. Two shapes only: a tinted track for choosing one of a set, and a bordered strip for actions that belong together. Variants: segmented, attached, icon-toolbar, split, input, vertical, responsive, django.
- **Dropdown menu** `dropdown` — A menu of actions anchored to a trigger. Real focus walks the items one tabindex="-1" at a time; destructive items sit last, below a divider. Variants: default, row-actions, groups, checkbox-items, radio-items, shortcuts, submenu, destructive, account.

### Forms

- **Label** `label` — The name of a control, bound to it with for and id or by wrapping it. The smallest component here, and the one that is most often drawn rather than connected. Variants: default, required, wrapping, legend, trailing, hidden, states, horizontal, caption.
- **Field** `field` — Label, control, help text and error in one block. This is the unit every form is built from, and the thing that owns the wiring between the four. Variants: default, error, required, horizontal, group, choice, action, grid, readonly.
- **Input** `input` — Single-line text entry. The border lives on the wrapper, not on the control, so an icon, a unit or a clear button sits inside the focus outline instead of beside it. Variants: default, sizes, icon, amount, search, error, format, password, disabled.
- **Input group** `input-group` — One text field and the things that qualify it — a unit, a currency, a scope select, an action — inside a single bordered enclosure that draws one focus outline for all of them. Variants: default, icon, button, select, action, search, textarea, error, dense.
- **Select** `select` — One answer out of a short fixed list. A real <select>, styled through its wrapper the way an input is, and an Alpine listbox only for the rows an <option> cannot hold. Variants: default, groups, states, multiple, filter, rich, status, cascade, django.
- **Textarea** `textarea` — Multi-line text entry. Same bordered wrapper as the input, a height measured in rows, and a counter when there is a limit worth showing. Variants: default, sizes, counter, autogrow, toolbar, error, disabled, django.
- **Checkbox** `checkbox` — An independent on or off — one flag, a set of options, or the row selection a register's bulk actions run on. A real native box wearing accent-zinc-700. Variants: default, group, indeterminate, cards, filters, table, states, django.
- **Radio** `radio` — One of a set, and exactly one. Real native radios wearing accent-zinc-700, where the shared name is the group and the only way to mean none is an option that says so. Variants: default, descriptions, cards, inline, none, table, states, django.
- **Toggle** `toggle` — A setting that takes effect the moment it is touched. A real checkbox carrying role="switch", with the track and the thumb beside it painted by peer-checked utilities. Variants: default, sizes, list, group, inline, states, htmx, django.
- **Combobox** `combobox` — A text box that filters a list of records and commits one of them. The typing is a search; what reaches the server is a hidden input under it. Variants: default, multi, select-all, groups, rich, remote, create, states, django.
- **Attachment** `attachment` — The documents hanging off a record — a drop zone over the list of what is already there. Every file shows its type, size, who attached it and when. Variants: default, empty, uploading, rejected, readonly, single, images, django.
- **Calendar** `calendar` — A month grid for picking a date or a range. Monday-first, tabular figures, and the same graphite selection the rest of the system uses. Variants: month, picker, range, jump, constrained, presets, native, django.
- **Questionnaire** `questionnaire` — A run of questions answered in order on one page — a QC checklist, a vendor assessment, a safety audit. One fieldset per question, the question text as its legend, and three equal tiles carrying the answer so a column of them can be read at a glance. Variants: question, run, observation, conditional, scale, multi, sheet, invalid, signed.

### Data display

- **Table** `table` — Rows of records with a sortable header. The workhorse of every register screen — order lists, GRN lists, ledgers. Variants: default, selection, row-actions, dense, responsive.
- **Data table** `data-table` — The register screen assembled: a table with a search box, sortable headers, column visibility, row selection and a pager, all running off one array of records. Variants: default, compact, server.
- **Pagination** `pagination` — Moves through a long register a page at a time, and says where you are in it. The range and the total are the component; the arrows are only what you do about them. Variants: simple, numbered, range, page-size, dense, edges, loading, load-more, footer.
- **Stat card** `stat-card` — One number that matters, with the label above it and the change since the last period below. The tile a dashboard strip is made of, and the answer whenever the data is a single current value rather than a shape. Variants: default, delta, sparkline, grid, status, dense, loading, empty, dashboard.
- **Chart** `chart` — Chart.js on a canvas, wearing this system's colours. The legend is HTML and doubles as the palette the canvas paints from, so a swatch and the line it names cannot drift apart. Variants: setup, line, bar, horizontal, stacked, donut, sparkline, empty, django.
- **Progress** `progress` — The determinate wait. A graphite rail filled to the fraction of a known total that is done — receipt against an order, lines closed on a GRN, quantity built against a plan — with the two figures written out beside it. Variants: bar, bare, steps, inline, tones, stacked, radial, indeterminate, production.
- **Empty state** `empty-state` — What a region shows when it has nothing to draw. Four different situations wearing one shape — nothing created yet, nothing matching the query, nothing this account may see, and nothing that loaded — and the whole job of the component is saying which one it is. Variants: nothing-yet, no-results, filtered, error, permission, in-table, compact, inline-create, register.
- **Skeleton** `skeleton` — Grey blocks standing in the exact box the content will occupy — same rows, same leading, same column widths — so the first paint of a screen whose layout is already known lands without moving. Variants: text, heading, table, card, stats, list, form, chart, record.
- **Marker** `marker` — The mark that opens a list item — a dot, a number, an icon or a tinted well — drawn as a real element in a box the height of one line, so it holds its place when the item wraps. Variants: prose, dot, numbered, checklist, timeline, register, nested, steps, dense.
- **Spinner** `spinner` — The indeterminate wait. A graphite ring that turns while work of unknown length is in flight, and a line of text that says what the work is. Variants: default, sizes, label, panel, inline, overlay, delayed, states, django.

### Feedback

- **Alert** `alert` — An inline notice about the page or the record in front of the user. White card, zinc border, and the only colour is the icon. Variants: tags, compact, dismissible, action, records, progress, banner, form-errors, django.
- **Toast** `toast` — A short confirmation that an action the user just took has finished, pushed into a live region pinned to the bottom-left and gone a few seconds later. It reports an outcome; it is never where the outcome is recorded. Variants: default, tones, undo, link, error, stack, pending, dismiss-all, posting.
- **Alert dialog** `alert-dialog` — A dialog that interrupts to ask one question with two answers. Unlike a plain dialog it does not dismiss on a backdrop click — the user has to choose. Variants: confirm, destructive, typed, bulk, unsaved.
- **Dialog** `dialog` — A centred, dismissible panel over a dimmed page. Use it to take a handful of fields without leaving the list. Variants: form, scrolling, reference.
- **Sheet** `sheet` — A panel that slides in from the right over the page. Shows a record, or the filters for a list, without losing the user's place in it. Variants: record, filters.
- **Drawer** `drawer` — A panel that rises from the bottom edge, sized to its content and capped short of the viewport. The phone-shaped place to put a short action list or a quick filter, because the bottom of the screen is where the thumb already is. Variants: actions, filter, long.
- **Badge** `badge` — A small pill that labels a record — status, tag or count. Every pill is the same graphite shape; a 6px dot carries the colour. Variants: status, inline, sizes, icon, filter, removable, count, table, django.
- **Tooltip** `tooltip` — A short dark bubble that names the control under the pointer or under the keyboard. It carries a label and nothing else — no controls, no facts that are not already somewhere the user can reach without hovering. Variants: icon, placement, truncated, shortcut, disabled, table, arrow, delay-group, row-actions.
- **Hovercard** `hovercard` — A card of record detail that opens under a link on hover or focus, after a deliberate delay, and stays open long enough to be read and clicked. Variants: default, vendor, user, placement, htmx, loading, error, mobile, django.
- **Popover** `popover` — A panel of controls anchored to a button and opened by a click. It holds things you focus and operate — a filter, a column list, a date range, a two-field edit — and the page behind it keeps working. Variants: default, filter, columns, date-range, inline-edit, arrow, placement, responsive, htmx.
- **Avatar** `avatar` — Initials in a circle standing in for a person. There are no photographs in this system, so a zinc tint and two letters is the whole thing. Variants: sizes, self, with-name, stacked, in-row, presence, menu, placeholder.

### Navigation

- **Tabs** `tabs` — Switches between views of the same record without leaving the page. The panel below changes; the row above is a widget, not a menu, and the keyboard has to know the difference. Variants: underline, pill, scrollable, vertical, url, lazy, states, django.
- **Breadcrumbs** `breadcrumbs` — The path from the section root down to the record on screen. The last crumb says where you are and is not a link. Variants: default, record, truncated, overflow, responsive, page-header, back, django.
- **Menubar** `menubar` — A row of menus across the top of a document — File, Edit, View — sharing one tab stop and one keyboard model. A desktop-application affordance, and most internal screens should not have one. Variants: default, shortcuts, checks, submenu, states, dense, collapsed, trailing, htmx.
- **Navigation menu** `navigation-menu` — A horizontal bar of links to places, some of which open a panel of more links. Every item is an anchor, so the browser's own navigation gestures keep working, and aria-current says which one you are on. Variants: links, panel, columns, featured, icons, mixed, current, phone, htmx.
- **Sidebar** `sidebar` — The primary navigation panel of the console: a header, grouped menus with counts and submenus, and a footer for the signed-in user. It has three forms — a 256px panel, a 68px icon rail, and an off-canvas sheet over the page. Variants: default, counts, nested, rail, flyout, collapse, mobile, blocks, skeleton.
- **Topbar** `topbar` — The application header above the page content: the sidebar trigger, the context you are working in, what you can search and who you are signed in as. A real <header> holding a named <nav>, sticky over the column and out of the way of everything that opens above it. Variants: default, search, account, toggle, context, compact, sticky, phone, assembled.
- **Accordion** `accordion` — Sections of content that collapse to their heading. The heading is a button that toggles the panel below it. Variants: default, single, cards.
- **Collapsible** `collapsible` — One trigger and one panel. The standalone disclosure — show more, an advanced section at the foot of a form, a filter bar that folds away. Variants: default, advanced, filters, native, card, controlled, states, django.
- **Command palette** `command-palette` — A ⌘K overlay for jumping to a record or firing an action by typing. It is a shortcut over the navigation, never the only route to something. Variants: default.

### Layout

- **App shell** `app-shell` — The page skeleton: an icon rail that expands to a labelled sidebar, a topbar carrying the hamburger, breadcrumb, command palette and account menu, and a single scrolling main column. Everything else in the app renders inside the main column. Variants: default.
- **Page header** `page-header` — The top block of a page: where it sits in the app, what it is, what state it is in, and what you can do to it. One h1 per page and it lives here. Variants: default, trail, record, tabs, filters, back, sticky, overflow.
- **Card** `card` — A bordered white panel that groups one thing. A header names it, the body holds the content, and an optional footer carries totals or actions. Variants: default, actions, stats, section, table, clickable, grid, empty, django.
- **Separator** `separator` — The rule that divides content. Almost always a border on the thing beside it rather than an element of its own, and almost always silent to a screen reader. Variants: default, rows, vertical, labelled, menu, django.
- **Carousel** `carousel` — A horizontal rail of items that snaps one item at a time. CSS scroll snap does the moving; the arrows and the counter are the only JavaScript. Variants: default, peek, dots, photo, thumbnails, stats, empty, django.
- **List and detail** `list-detail` — A queue on the left and the record being worked on beside it. Arrow keys walk the list, Enter opens the record into the detail pane, and only the two panes scroll — the page behind them does not move. Variants: default, nothing-selected, responsive, search, three-pane, loading, qc-hold.
- **Form page** `form-page` — The layout a create or edit screen uses: one h1, the fields grouped in cards, a validation summary that links to every field that failed, and Save and Cancel where the user can always reach them. Variants: two-column, side-rail, sections, invalid, sticky-actions, line-items, wizard, readonly.
- **Auth page** `auth-page` — The signed-out screen: one centred card, the fewest fields that will do, and nothing else on the page. Sign in, the second factor after it, and every screen the user lands on when one of the two fails. Variants: signin, failed, forgot, sent, reset, otp, sso, locked.
- **Error page** `error-page` — The whole screen the user gets when the page could not be produced at all. It says what failed in their own terms, whether anything they did was saved, and gives one way back into an application whose navigation is not on this page. Variants: 404, 403, 500, maintenance, offline, expired, django.

## Machine-readable

Cost is why this is split, so the cost is on the label. Fetch the smallest
thing that answers the question.

| endpoint | size | cost | what it is |
|---|---|--:|---|
| [r/index.json](r/index.json) | 74 KB | ~21k tokens | The spec and every component summarised, with variant ids. No markup. The largest thing you are ever asked to fetch whole. |
| `r/<id>.json` | median 43 KB, largest 144 KB (`form-page`) | ~12k tokens / ~41k tokens | One component: rules, anatomy, behaviour, accessibility, and every variant with its html. |
| `r/<id>/<variant>.html` | median 4 KB, largest 45 KB (`app-shell/default`) | ~1k tokens / ~13k tokens | The markup, raw. No JSON envelope, no escaping, paste as-is. |
| [registry.json](registry.json) | 2.5 MB | ~729k tokens | Everything at once. **Do not fetch this.** It is roughly 4× a 200k context window and exists only so older integrations do not break. |

The component list above prints every variant id, so once you have read this
file you can build a variant URL yourself and skip r/index.json entirely:
`GET /r/button/variants.html` returns the markup for button/variants and nothing
else. That is the common path — one read of llms.txt, then a few small ones.

Read the ids; do not guess them. Only 32 of the 55 components have a variant
called `default`, and 23 do not, so a guessed URL is a 404 rather
than a fallback. The ids are listed above precisely because they are not
predictable from the component name.
